correctness.rationale: PASS: For balanced arms and strictly positive 2×2 cells, 1≤t<c≤m−1, write d=c−t; ARR=d/m, NNT=m/d and RRR=d/c. Strict reversal ⇔ (d1−d2)(d1/c1−d2/c2)<0. Independent exhaustive exact Fraction enumeration yields for m=2..6 admissible counts 0,1,3,6,10 and reversal-pair counts 0,0,0,0,2. Both pairs at m=6 are (1,2) vs (3,5) and (1,3) vs (2,5). Explicit (1,2) vs (m−3,m−1) persists all m≥6, since 1/m<2/m but 1/2>2/(m−1). The all-m conclusion is analytic, not inferred from finite sample replay.

value.rationale: PASS: The strict-reversal phenomenon matters to comparison of clinical effect sizes: the integer minimum m=6 with all four cells positive rules out misleading degenerate zero-event examples and gives the earliest complete, exact two-witness classification plus persistent family. The exact cutoff is a motivated small-instance invariant for pedagogy and benchmark design; no claim of clinical significance at sample size six or inferential treatment superiority.
residual_risks: Balanced equal arm size and all four positive cells are essential; point estimates only, no confidence intervals or clinical inference.

scientific_limitations: Equal arms, t<c, no zero cells; estimates only, no sampling uncertainty, no statistical inference, no claim that one risk metric is clinically always preferable.
